definition: Encoding specificity is the degree to which a to-be-remembered cue is encoded in a detailed, specific way rather than a general, non-specific way. In prospective memory tasks, more specific cue encoding is associated with better remembering to carry out a planned action when the cue appears.

reasons: The packet supports cue-encoding specificity in event-based prospective memory, but it does not establish a general definition of “encoding specificity” as a broad memory principle.
The claim that a cue is encoded in a “detailed, specific way rather than a general, non-specific way” goes beyond the packet’s wording and is not directly supported as a definition.

The packet discusses “cue-encoding specificity (specific cue vs. non-specific cue)” in event-based prospective memory, but it does not explicitly define “specific” as encoding “in a detailed, specific way rather than a general, non-specific way,” so this detailed/detailed-vs-general characterization is not directly supported.

The definition’s first sentence generalizes “to-be-remembered cue” as a broad memory process, while the packet only frames cue specificity within event-based prospective memory (remembering planned actions in response to target cues).
